Diagnosis: `unified.qk_norm` was the largest redundant scope. Its `q_input_copy` and `k_input_copy` elementwise leaves had empty semantic mappings and zero necessary work; `q_norm` and `k_norm` remained required (`pred.casev0.optimality-kernel-ladder`, `pred.casev1.optimality-kernel-ladder`).

Fix: Commit `058a97e4cdb2e2e4ea9149e67b347cc04b11a6b2` sets `BeforeRecipe::COPY_INPUTS` to `false`, removes the two matching location-map entries, and makes timing-predict strictly cache-only by removing its JIT enable call.

Evidence: Before scope R0/R5/R6/R7 were `0.00047138 / 0.000088768495375 / 0.000000001792 / 0.000000001792` GPU-seconds with four leaves; see [before report](logs/eval_before_run/reports/optimality_scoped_label_unified_qk_norm_qknormlocalworklet_local_1_gpu_qo_num_qo_head_8c0386ce0dd1.json) and `pred.casev0.operationv0.cost-tree`. After they were `0.000272748 / 0.0000443842525 / 0.000000001792 / 0.000000001792` with only `q_norm` and `k_norm`; see [after report](logs/eval_after_run/reports/optimality_scoped_label_unified_qk_norm_qknormlocalworklet_local_1_gpu_qo_num_qo_head_d91345dfbf18.json) and `pred.casev0.operationv0.cost-tree`. Exactly the two copy leaves disappeared, all other leaves stayed unchanged, and R6/R7 were identical.

Both predictions completed with `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=''` and no profiling flag. The after run used an isolated equivalent config at `logs/eval_after_run` to preserve the before Analyzer resource. Focused simulator tests and `git diff --check` passed; rustfmt was unavailable.

judge.reasoning: The agent independently identified qk_norm's redundant q/k input copies, matching the ground-truth non-contiguous Q/K RMSNorm copy bottleneck. Disabling COPY_INPUTS removes exactly those copies while preserving q_norm and k_norm, so the implemented fix has the same effect.
